The ideal candidate brings healthcare call center experience, a clear and empathetic communication style, and the ability to work accurately across multiple systems in a fast-moving environment.

Key Responsibilities

• Answer inbound calls promptly across patient queues and route callers to the appropriate team when needed

• Schedule, reschedule, and confirm new and returning patient appointments for both in-office and telehealth visits

• Verify and update patient demographic and insurance information accurately at each point of contact

• Return voicemails and respond to patient messages via the practice messaging platform within the same business day

• Warm-transfer billing and insurance inquiries to the appropriate internal team

• Maintain a professional, patient, and empathetic manner across all patient interactions regardless of call volume or complexity
Systems
The practice uses Athena (EHR and scheduling), Klara (patient messaging), and Phreesia (patient intake). Prior experience with any of these platforms is a plus; full training will be provided.
Qualifications
Required

• Minimum 1 year of call center experience, preferably within a medical practice or healthcare setting

• Working knowledge of US health insurance, including commercial plans, Medicare, Medicare Advantage, and TRICARE

• Clear, professional, and empathetic phone manner - patients may be anxious, in pain, or frustrated, and composure matters

• Strong attention to detail with the ability to accurately capture and update patient information while managing an active call

• Comfortable working simultaneously across multiple platforms and systems

• Reliable high-speed internet connection and a quiet, dedicated home workspace suitable for patient calls
Preferred

• Experience with Athena, Klara, or Phreesia

• Prior experience scheduling telehealth appointments in addition to in-office visits

• Familiarity with HIPAA requirements and patient privacy standards in a remote work context
Schedule and Start Date

• Full-time: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Central Time

• Fully remote

• Target start date: November 1, 2026
What We Are Looking For
Patients calling a medical practice are not calling because everything is going well. The Medical Patient Representative is often the first voice a patient hears, and the tone of that interaction sets the tone for their entire experience with the practice. The right candidate understands this and approaches every call with care, accuracy, and professionalism - whether it is a routine appointment confirmation or a frustrated patient with an unresolved concern.
You are organized, detail-oriented, and reliable. You follow through on messages the same day, you document what you do, and you make sure patients leave the interaction feeling heard and taken care of. Healthcare experience is important here - not just because of the systems, but because of the stakes.

This is a full time role
Up to $6/hr

description: Description QuantumDiamonds is a novel equipment vendor from Germany which builds magnetic field imaging systems based on quantum sensors. Our Data Science & Machine Learning team in Pre-Development owns the chain from raw quantum sensor data to the current map an engineer can act on: the statistical evaluation of the sensor signal, the simulation and training data pipelines, the reconstruction of fields and currents, with the machine learning pipeline for three-dimensional current in production today, and the validation of every map against simulation and reference measurements. We are looking for a Data Scientist to own one question for the team: can we trust this map, and if not, where in the chain did it go wrong? Every measurement, in our lab or at a customer, gets a verdict and a reason. You build the checks that produce it, keep the catalogue of known artifacts and reference measurements behind it, and make it automatic for the routine cases so that your judgement goes to the hard ones. When a check fails, you trace it to its source in the chain, fix it when it sits in the evaluation, and drive the fix with the owning engineer when it does not. Our Applications engineers, who run the customer projects, rely on your verdict for what reaches the customer. A senior data scientist on the team backs you on the hard calls at the start; the aim is that you become the owner of this question. This is a hands-on analysis role, not a research position: the data is real, the chain is in daily use, and every improvement you make shows up in the next measurement. Your background does not need to be in quantum sensing or semiconductors: if you have learned to tell signal from noise, calibration errors and artifacts in another demanding measurement system, we want to hear from you.

Leverage your hands-on experience to build authentic debugging and feature challenges within real game projects, directly impacting how AI agents learn to analyze, play, and develop games. • Design and build small-scale game projects or interactive scenes in a major game engine to serve as the foundation for assessment tasks.

• Integrate realistic gameplay bugs that require thorough playtesting and on-screen analysis to discover and resolve.

• Develop multifaceted gameplay feature challenges that rely on multiple in-game systems and mechanics.

• Draft clear and concise briefs for each task, emulating the style of instructions from players, designers, or producers.

• Create comprehensive reference solutions-including both bug fixes and feature implementations-for every assignment.

• Define detailed success criteria, including input sequences, expected visual outcomes, and verifiable in-game states.

• Conduct end-to-end playtesting of each task to guarantee reliability and solvability.

• Demonstrated experience in game development, whether in AAA, indie, solo, or serious hobby contexts.

• A portfolio or verifiable published work (personal site, itch.io, Steam, GitHub, game jam entries, or shipped title credits). Your portfolio is the most important part of your application and plays a major role in our selection, so please include the work that best represents your skills.

• Comfort with engine scripting languages such as C#, GDScript, C++, or Blueprints, with the ability to interpret, troubleshoot, and enhance gameplay logic.

• Proven ability to identify and resolve gameplay issues through iterative playtesting.

• Strong written communication skills for drafting precise task instructions and acceptance criteria.

• Experience in game QA, technical design, systems design, automated testing, or prior contribution to AI evaluation projects is a plus.

Compensation Structure
Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete work may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow. Minimum submission requirements apply. Experts must submit a minimum of tasks per week.
